text: Ghulam Mohammed Sadiq (1912 – 1971) was an Indian politician who served as the Prime Minister of Jammu and Kashmir from 1964 to 1965, when the position was officially renamed to Chief Minister due to the amendment of the J&K Constitution by the then Congress government through the Sixth Constitution of J&K Amendment Act, 1965. He continued in office as Chief Minister until his death in 1971. Sadiq graduated from Islamia College in Lahore and Aligarh Muslim University. He served in Sheikh Abdullah's first cabinet from 1947 to 1953. He led the National Conference party from 1957 to 1961 before joining the Indian National Congress. He was elected Prime Minister of Jammu and Kashmir in 1964 and became the first Chief Minister of the state following the constitutional amendment in 1965. He died in office on 12 December 1971 due to a heart attack. This article about an Indian National Congress politician from Jammu and Kashmir is a stub.
